register.name: Resilience and Productive Safety Nets Program
register.detail: World Bank · Program-for-Results · Appraisal document of 19 May 2026 · IDA credit €19.7 million, grant SDR 5.6 million · Signed 21 August 2026, as reported
register.note: IDA share of $249 million in all, with $15 million from the OPEC Fund and $199 million from the Government
register.text: A Program-for-Results that strengthens the efficiency, timeliness and productive focus of Mauritania’s adaptive social protection system for poor and vulnerable households, including refugees and host communities. It serves food and livelihood for the poorest families, when droughts and other shocks strike.

register.name: Extended Credit Facility and Extended Fund Facility, 2026
register.detail: IMF · Approved 24 June 2026 · 42 months · SDR 70.82 million, 55 percent of quota · SDR 78.78 million (about US$105.6 million) made available at once
register.text: Building on the 2022–2026 programme: institutions, human capital and governance of public enterprises.
register.note: With the fifth and final review of the Resilience and Sustainability Facility

register.name: IQRAA, quality, results and access to education for all
register.detail: World Bank · Program-for-Results · Release of 18 June 2026 · $40 million from IDA, $17.53 million from the Global Partnership for Education
register.note: The first Program-for-Results in Mauritania’s education sector
register.text: The first Program-for-Results in Mauritania’s education sector finances better basic education, wider access to secondary school, above all for adolescent girls, and schooling in areas that host refugees. It is expected to reach more than 1.3 million pupils and to bring more than 125,000 refugee children into the national school system. Education is the standard furthest from reach in Mauritania.

register.name: West Africa Coastal Areas (WACA+), Phase 1
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 17 March 2026 · With Benin · $207 million from IDA, $5 million from PROBLUE, $28 million of private capital
register.text: The first phase of the West Africa Coastal Areas programme, for Benin and Mauritania, reduces the exposure of more than 530,000 people to coastal erosion and floods and is expected to create about 13,000 better-paid jobs. In Mauritania it reinforces the dune belt that shields Nouakchott and offers a partial portfolio credit guarantee to unlock up to $20 million of new lending for fish processing enterprises.

register.name: First Reform for Inclusive and Sustainable Growth Development Policy Financing
register.detail: World Bank · Approved, release of 25 November 2025 · IDA credit · First in a programmatic series of three
register.text: Budget support tied to reforms that strengthen property tax collection and the rules for private investment, build human capital and skills for jobs, and widen access to affordable and sustainable energy. It serves livelihood, education and energy.

register.name: West Africa Regional Electricity Market Program, Phase 1: Mauritania Transmission Corridor
register.text: High-voltage lines that tie Mauritania into the West African power market, so its wind and sun can be sold to its neighbours.

register.name: Development of Energy Resources and Mining Sector Support (DREAM), Phase 1
register.text: Prepares green hydrogen, energy storage and the mining sector to grow, with private investment to follow.

register.name: Mauritania Public Spending Efficiency
register.text: Makes public spending go further in health, education and social protection; US$42 million paid for results.

register.name: Rural Electrification Project in isolated areas
register.detail: IsDB · Financing agreement signed at the 2026 IsDB Group Annual Meetings, Baku · Release of 19 June 2026
register.note: To connect 22,000 households and 3,000 socio-economic facilities
register.text: A financing agreement to bring electricity to isolated areas of Mauritania. It is to connect 22,000 households and 3,000 socio-economic facilities in remote regions, for energy.

register.name: Integrated referral hospital, Nouakchott
register.detail: IsDB · Signed in Jeddah · Reported 11 March 2026 · One of two agreements worth €116.6 million
register.note: Reported by The North Africa Post; the IsDB’s own release was not opened
register.text: Finances the construction and equipping of an integrated referral hospital in Nouakchott. It serves health, on which Mauritania scores 40 of 100 on the WHO index of essential service coverage.

register.name: Mauritania–Mali electricity interconnection
register.detail: IsDB · Signed in Jeddah · Reported 11 March 2026 · One of two agreements worth €116.6 million
register.note: Reported by The North Africa Post; the IsDB’s own release was not opened
register.text: Supports the interconnection of the electricity grid between Mauritania and Mali. It serves energy: Mauritanians use about 458 kWh of electricity a person a year.

register.name: 3R-Water, rural water resilience
register.detail: AfDB · Transition Support Facility · Concessional loan · Signed at the 2025 Annual Meetings, Abidjan · Release of 29 May 2025
register.note: Brakna, Tagant and Adrar; more than 450,000 people
register.text: A concessional loan that expands access to rural water for domestic, productive and ecosystem uses, with solar-powered drinking water systems, pastoral watering stations and latrine blocks in 124 schools and 23 health centres. It is expected to reach more than 450,000 people, most of them women and young people.

register.name: Women’s market gardens, Climate Action Window
register.detail: AfDB · African Development Fund, Climate Action Window · Grant · Signed at the 2025 Annual Meetings, Abidjan · Release of 29 May 2025
register.text: A grant for gender-sensitive agriculture and women’s entrepreneurship that finances the development and equipping of market garden perimeters for women-led cooperatives. It serves food and livelihood.

register.name: Vocational training and youth employability
register.detail: IsDB · Signed at the 2025 Annual Meetings, Algiers · Release of 21 May 2025
register.note: Signed by the Minister of Economy and Finance
register.text: A financing agreement to support vocational training and youth employability. It aims to give young people the skills the job market requires, for livelihood and education.

register.name: Health Sector Support Programme (PASS IV)
register.detail: European Union · Signed 15 June 2026 · One of two programmes worth €40 million in all
register.text: A programme that strengthens Mauritania’s health system, including its health infrastructure. It serves health, on which Mauritania scores 40 of 100 on the WHO index of essential service coverage.

register.name: Frontières Sud, the southern border regions
register.detail: European Union · Signed 15 June 2026 · MRU 1.16 billion · One of two programmes worth €40 million in all
register.note: Water and rural electrification by photovoltaic mini-grids
register.text: A programme for the southern border regions whose investments include access to water and rural electrification by photovoltaic mini-grids. It serves water and energy.

register.name: Japanese Food Assistance Programme, fiscal year 2024
register.detail: Japan · Grant · About 4,331 tonnes of rice received 26 January 2026 · About MRU 150 million
register.note: The proceeds of the rice sale fund food aid through the Food Security Commission
register.text: A grant of rice from the people of Japan, received in Nouakchott in January 2026. The counterpart fund from its sale finances the Government’s food distribution, through the Food Security Commission, to vulnerable people in emergencies.

register.name: Global Gateway budget support programme
register.detail: European Union · Launched 19 December 2024 · €95 million to the national budget, €5 million of institutional support · First disbursement €23 million
register.note: Green hydrogen, migration and forced displacement, and health
register.text: Budget support for Mauritania’s public policies on green hydrogen, migration and forced displacement, and health, including universal health coverage by 2030. It also aims to open employment and education opportunities.

register.name: 60 MW hybrid solar and wind plant, Iwa Green Energy
register.detail: Independent power producer contract · AfDB release of 1 October 2025 · Desert to Power · Fully private financing · Operation scheduled for September 2026
register.note: Mauritania’s first independent power producer contract
register.text: Mauritania’s first independent power producer contract, with Iwa Green Energy, for a 60-megawatt hybrid solar and wind plant. Its fully private financing is to expand an installed capacity of about 450 megawatts without adding to public debt, for energy.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Coast
items.label: Committed to the coast with Benin, 2026
items.text: One of the richest fishing grounds of the Atlantic, now protected and financed as a blue economy.

items.name: The Ground
items.label: Of GDP from natural resource rents, 2021
items.text: Iron ore and gold earn today, with gas from the Greater Tortue Ahmeyim field shared with Senegal.

items.name: The Land
items.label: Land area, 2024
items.text: Territory to farm, mine, power and protect.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2024
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 42.4% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: Hodere Pinnal cooperative
items.text: A cooperative of 20 women in Nouakchott that turns millet, rice, maize, beans and watermelon seeds into a nutritious powdered mix, selling up to 20 jars a day in Ramadan.

items.name: Teydouma cooperative
items.text: A women’s camel milk cooperative, founded in 2019, that pasteurises and bottles camel milk and makes camel cheese.

items.name: Learniverse
items.text: An edtech start-up that uses virtual reality to bring immersive, curriculum-aligned content to underserved schools, the final winner of the 2025 Ra’idat programme for women-led businesses.

items.name: EcoRice
items.text: A women-led business of the 2025 Ra’idat cohort that makes low-cost poultry feed from recycled rice by-products.

items.name: PROCAPEC
items.text: A microfinance network, one of three that lend directly to artisanal fishing operations, under rules that cap a loan at USD 12,500 a project.
